definition: Colloquial verb meaning to have an erection; literally 'to stand,' used in phrases such as 'у него стоит' (he's hard).
notes: Imperfective aspect denotes ongoing erect state. Transparent body-position metaphor. Paired with perfective встать for the onset of erection.

definition: Colloquial perfective verb meaning to get an erection; literally 'to stand up/rise,' as in 'у него встал' (he got hard).
notes: Perfective aspect marks the transition to erection rather than the sustained state. Aspectual pair of стоять. Equally common and equally non-stigmatized in informal speech.

definition: Colloquial verb meaning to stick out or protrude; in sexual context describes an erect or visibly prominent penis.
notes: Broad polysemy beyond sex: also means to jut out, to be high on drugs (slang). In sexual use it foregrounds protrusion/visibility. Slightly more crude than стоять because the visual image is more explicit.

definition: Sexual arousal or excitement; the physical and psychological state of being turned on; used both clinically and in everyday speech.
notes: Polysemous: equally standard for non-sexual excitement (crowd agitation, nervous energy). Clinical texts and popular discourse use the same word without register shift.

definition: Orgasm; the climax of sexual excitement; direct loanword from Greek/Latin via European languages, fully naturalized in Russian.
notes: Entered Russian in the 20th century. Used without stigma across medical, popular-science, and colloquial registers. No strong crude valence; primarily a technical loanword repurposed colloquially.

definition: Euphemism for sexual release or orgasm; literally 'discharge' or 'tension release'; polysemous with the political term for Cold War détente.
notes: The détente meaning (разрядка напряжённости) is equally well-known. Sexual usage exploits the identical mechanics of tension-discharge. Low crude score reflects the euphemistic distance from explicit vocabulary.

definition: Noun form of the crude slang verb кончать/кончить (to cum); refers to orgasm or ejaculation, predominantly in male contexts.
notes: The underlying verb кончать (to finish) is one of the most common Russian sexual slang verbs. The noun кончание is less frequent than the verb itself but fully understood. Also carries the non-sexual meaning of 'ending/finishing.'

definition: Russian loanword from English 'cumshot'; the pornographic depiction of visible external male ejaculation.
notes: Opaque to older and porn-naive speakers. Recognized primarily among younger demographics and online pornography consumers. Spelling varies (камшот / кам-шот).

definition: Russian loanword from English 'creampie'; ejaculation inside a partner's vagina or anus without a condom, or the visible result.
notes: Narrow reach: mainly used in online pornography forums and communities. Not recognized by a general adult audience. Transliteration reflects approximate Russian phonology of the English source.

definition: Clinical/technical loanword for vaginal lubrication; the secretion of moisture by the vaginal walls during sexual arousal.
notes: Primarily clinical and educational register. General population more likely to use descriptive phrases. Also used for mechanical lubrication (engines, machinery), which shares the same Russian word.

definition: Adjective meaning sexually aroused or excited; adjectival form of возбуждение; equally valid in non-sexual contexts for general excitement.
notes: Same polysemy as the noun: 'возбуждённая толпа' = excited crowd, not a sexual crowd. The ё (yo) vowel is often written as е in informal text, producing 'возбужденный.'

definition: Adjective meaning lustful or lascivious; describing a person driven by excessive or overt sexual desire; carries a pejorative and judgmental tone.
notes: Derived from похоть (lust). Typically applied to others as a condemnation rather than self-applied. More elevated and literary than colloquial equivalents; frequency declining in everyday speech.

definition: Adjective meaning dissolute, licentious, or sexually immoral; implying chronic promiscuity and moral laxity.
notes: Etymological root of the historical figure's nickname Rasputin (Распутин). Implies not just occasional transgression but habitual moral looseness. Somewhat dated in everyday speech but widely recognized.

definition: Adjective meaning depraved, debauched, or morally corrupt; implies active sexual corruption slightly stronger than распутный.
notes: From развращать (to corrupt/deprave). Carries an implication of having been corrupted or of corrupting others, not merely of personal indulgence. Stronger moral weight than распутный.

definition: Archaic adjective meaning wanton, lecherous, or given to fornication; derived from блуд (fornication), carrying strong religious-moral overtones.
notes: From Old Church Slavonic блудъ (fornication; also wandering/straying from righteousness). Still appears in historical and religious texts. General recognition is lower among speakers under 40. Note: блудливая кошка = a cat that strays; the animal idiom kept some currency.

definition: Colloquial adjective literally meaning 'preoccupied' or 'worried,' but so thoroughly adopted as slang for sex-obsessed that the sexual sense dominates in informal speech.
notes: Classic Russian semantic shift: the formal word for 'concerned/preoccupied' became slang for someone preoccupied specifically with sex. Context usually disambiguates but in informal speech the sexual reading is the default assumption.

definition: Adjective meaning passionate or ardent; in romantic and sexual contexts describes intense, fervent desire or physical expression.
notes: Positive connotation; страстный поцелуй = passionate kiss. Applies equally to non-sexual contexts (a passionate speaker, a passionate love of music). Not inherently condemning; low crude score reflects cultural neutrality.

definition: Noun meaning lust or carnal desire; intense sexual appetite used in both secular literary and Orthodox religious-moral contexts.
notes: In Orthodox theology, похоть is one of the passions (страсти) to be overcome. The moral-condemnatory register is therefore always latent even in secular literary use. Root shared with похотливый.

definition: Noun meaning intense longing or sexual craving; more poetic and elevated than похоть, with emphasis on yearning rather than moral condemnation.
notes: High-register literary term used by Tolstoy, Dostoevsky, and other canonical authors. The yearning quality distinguishes it from the more condemnatory похоть. Active use declining in contemporary speech; primarily recognized through literary exposure.

definition: Noun meaning voluptuousness or sensuality; literally 'sweet passion'; describes abandoned, pleasurable indulgence in carnal sensation.
notes: Compound of сладкий (sweet) + страсть (passion). Classic 19th-century literary register; sharply less common in contemporary speech. English 'voluptuousness' and 'sensuality' are only approximate — the Russian retains a heady, almost intoxicated quality the English lacks.

definition: Adjective meaning voluptuous, sensuous, or pleasure-seeking; the adjectival form of сладострастие, used to describe a sensuous gaze, voluptuous form, or lascivious manner.
notes: Adjectival counterpart of сладострастие. Marked decline in active use compared to 19th-century literature; recognized mainly by readers of classical Russian texts or educated speakers.

definition: Noun meaning passion; intense consuming emotion including romantic desire, sexual appetite, or zealous drive; a foundational term in Russian romantic discourse.
notes: One of the most versatile high-frequency emotional nouns in Russian. In sexual contexts страсть implies consuming, uncontrollable desire. Not inherently vulgar — the low crude score reflects its use across registers without stigma.

definition: Noun meaning desire or wish; in sexual contexts the standard neutral term for wanting or desiring another person.
notes: Fully neutral: equally valid for 'I desire you' and 'I want a new car.' No moral loading. Sexual reading is entirely context-dependent; the word itself carries no sexual valence.

definition: Verb meaning to want; the phrase 'я хочу тебя' (I want you) is the most common everyday Russian expression of sexual desire.
notes: The standard 'to want' verb with no inherent sexual meaning; sexual reading entirely dependent on object ('тебя' = you). Slightly blunter register than желать in sexual contexts due to everyday directness. Very slightly higher crude score than желать for this reason.

definition: Verb meaning to desire or wish for; in sexual contexts a more literary and intense-sounding form of хотеть; 'я желаю тебя' = I desire you.
notes: More elevated register than хотеть; желать sounds more deliberate, poetic, or formal in a sexual context. Both verbs take the genitive of the person desired ('тебя'), but желать is more marked stylistically and less colloquial.
